Let \( \mathcal{M} \) be the Zariski open subset of the projective space \( \mathbb{P}^{19} \) that parametrizes smooth **canonical curves of genus 4**, i.e. smooth curves \( C \subset \mathbb{P}^3 \) that are complete intersections of a quadric surface and a cubic surface.  

Define the incidence variety  

\[
Z \;=\; \{\, (C, \Pi) \mid C \in \mathcal{M},\; \Pi \subset \mathbb{P}^3 \text{ is a plane that meets } C \text{ with multiplicity } \ge 2 \text{ at three distinct points} \,\}.
\]

Let \( \pi : Z \to \mathcal{M} \) be the projection onto the first factor.  
It is known that for a general curve \( C \) there are only finitely many such planes \( \Pi \) and that the map \( \pi \) is finite étale over a dense open subset \( V \subset \mathcal{M} \).

Define  

\[
L \;=\; \lim_{p\to\infty}\;
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_p)}
\sum_{C\in V(\mathbb{F}_p)} \#\pi^{-1}(C),
\]

the limiting average number of tritangent planes of a smooth genus‑4 canonical curve over the finite field \( \mathbb{F}_p \).

Compute \(\displaystyle \big\lfloor 100\,L \big\rfloor\).

Let \(V=\mathbf P\bigl(H^{0}(\mathbf P^{2},\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{2}}(2))\bigr)\cong\mathbf P^{5}\) be the projective space whose points correspond to plane conics (not necessarily smooth).

Fix a smooth conic  

\[
C_{0}=\{\,Q_{0}(x,y,z)=0\,\}\subset\mathbf P^{2},
\qquad Q_{0}=a_{0}x^{2}+b_{0}y^{2}+c_{0}z^{2}+d_{0}xy+e_{0}xz+f_{0}yz .
\]

For a variable conic \(C=\{\,Q(x,y,z)=0\,\}\) with homogeneous quadratic form  

\[
Q= a x^{2}+b y^{2}+c z^{2}+d xy+e xz+f yz ,
\]

define  

\[
T(C_{0})=\{\,C\in V \mid C \text{ is tangent to } C_{0}\text{ at some point of } \mathbf P^{2}\,\}.
\]

---

**(a)** Show that the condition “\(C\) is tangent to \(C_{0}\)” can be expressed as a single homogeneous polynomial equation in the coefficients \((a,b,c,d,e,f)\) of \(Q\).  
Determine the degree \(d\) of this polynomial, i.e. the degree of the hypersurface \(T(C_{0})\subset V\).

*(Hint: a point of tangency is a point \([x:y:z]\) where \(Q_{0}=Q=0\) and the two gradient vectors are linearly dependent. Eliminate \([x:y:z]\) using resultants or Gröbner bases.)*

---

**(b)** Let \(C_{1},\dots ,C_{5}\) be five general smooth conics in \(\mathbf P^{2}\).  
Assuming the hypersurfaces \(T(C_{i})\) intersect transversely, compute the number of (complex) conics that are simultaneously tangent to all five given conics.

Give your answer as a single integer.

Let \(\mathbb P^5\) be the projective space that parametrises all plane conics (including singular ones) in \(\mathbf P^2\).  
For a fixed smooth conic \(C\subset\mathbf P^2\) the set  

\[
T_C=\{\,Q\in\mathbb P^5 \mid Q \text{ is tangent to } C\,\}
\]

is a hypersurface of degree \(2\) in \(\mathbb P^5\).

Let \(C_1,\dots ,C_5\subset\mathbf P^2\) be five smooth conics in general position.
Consider the subscheme  

\[
X = T_{C_1}\cap T_{C_2}\cap T_{C_3}\cap T_{C_4}\cap T_{C_5}\;\subset\;\mathbb P^5 .
\]

\(X\) parametrises all (possibly singular) plane conics that are tangent to each of the five given conics.

Using intersection theory (Chern classes, excess‑intersection formula, etc.), determine the total number of points of \(X\) counted with multiplicity.  Give the answer as an integer.

Let \( \mathbb{P}^{2} \) have homogeneous coordinates \([x:y:z]\).
For a fixed smooth cubic curve  

\[
C:\;F(x,y,z)=0 ,\qquad   F\in \mathbb{Z}[x,y,z] \text{ homogeneous of degree }3,
\]

consider the projective space  

\[
\mathcal{Q}= \mathbb{P}\bigl(H^{0}(\mathbb{P}^{2},\mathcal O_{\mathbb{P}^{2}}(2))\bigr)\cong \mathbf P^{5},
\]

whose points correspond to plane conics \(Q(x,y,z)=0\) (with \(Q\) a non‑zero homogeneous quadratic polynomial, considered up to scaling).

A conic \(Q=0\) is **tangent to \(C\)** if there exists a point \(p\in \mathbb{P}^{2}\) at which the two curves intersect with multiplicity at least 2; equivalently, \(p\) is a common zero of \(F\) and \(Q\) and the two tangent lines at \(p\) coincide.

1. Show that the set  

\[
T_{C}= \{\, [Q]\in \mathcal{Q}\mid Q=0 \text{ is tangent to } C \,\}
\]

is a hypersurface in \(\mathcal{Q}\) and determine its degree \(d\).

2. Let \(C_{1},\dots ,C_{5}\) be five *general* smooth cubic curves in \(\mathbb{P}^{2}\).  
Assuming the hypersurfaces \(T_{C_{i}}\subset \mathcal{Q}\) intersect transversely, compute the number \(N\) of (complex) conics that are simultaneously tangent to all five curves \(C_{1},\dots ,C_{5}\).

Give your final answer as a decimal number rounded to four decimal places.  

*(If the answer is an integer, write it with four decimal places, e.g. `7776.0000`.)*

Let  

* \(U\) be the quasiprojective variety over \(\mathbb{Q}\) parametrising **nodal rational plane cubic curves** (i.e. images of morphisms \(\mathbb{P}^{1}\to\mathbb{P}^{2}\) of degree 3 that have exactly one node and no other singularities).  

* \(W\subset U\times (\mathbb{P}^{2})^{8}\) be the closed subscheme consisting of tuples \((C,p_{1},\dots ,p_{8})\) such that each point \(p_{i}\) lies on the curve \(C\).

Let  

\[
\pi : W \longrightarrow (\mathbb{P}^{2})^{8}
\]

be the projection onto the second factor, and let \(V\subset (\mathbb{P}^{2})^{8}\) be the dense open subset over which \(\pi\) is finite étale (i.e. over which the eight points are in general position and no extra degeneracies occur).

For a prime \(p\) let \(V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) denote the set of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-rational points of \(V\). Define  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x).
\]

That is, \(L\) is the limit of the average number of nodal rational cubic curves passing through a generic ordered 8‑tuple of points of \(\mathbb{P}^{2}\) over \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\), as \(p\) tends to infinity.

Compute \(\displaystyle \bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor\).  

*(Give the integer answer.)*

Let  

\[
S\subset\mathbf{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{Z}}
\]

be the smooth cubic surface given by the homogeneous equation  

\[
X_{0}^{3}+X_{1}^{3}+X_{2}^{3}+X_{3}^{3}=0 .
\]

Denote by \(\mathcal{L}\) the scheme that parametrises lines contained in \(S\) (over any base field).  
Consider the incidence variety  

\[
Z=\{\,(\ell ,P)\mid \ell\in\mathcal{L},\; P\in\ell\,\}\subset\mathcal{L}\times \mathbf{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{Z}},
\]

and let  

\[
\pi : Z \longrightarrow S
\]

be the projection onto the second factor, \(\pi(\ell ,P)=P\).

It is known that for a smooth cubic surface over an algebraically closed field, through a **general** point of the surface there pass exactly six lines contained in the surface.

Let \(V\subset S\) be the dense open subscheme consisting of those points \(P\) for which \(\pi\) is étale (i.e., the fibre \(\pi^{-1}(P)\) consists of six distinct points).

For a prime \(p\) let \(V(\mathbb{F}_p)\) be the set of \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-rational points of \(V\). Define  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\;
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_p)}\;
\sum_{P\in V(\mathbb{F}_p)}\;\#\pi^{-1}(P).
\]

Compute \(\displaystyle\bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor\).

Let  

\[
\mathcal{P}= \mathbb{P}\bigl(H^{0}\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{2},\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{2}}(4)\bigr)\bigr)\cong\mathbb{P}^{14}
\]

be the projective space parametrising plane curves of degree 4.  
Denote by  

\[
U\subset\mathcal{P}
\]

the Zariski‑open subset consisting of smooth quartic curves.  

For a line \(\ell\subset\mathbb{P}^{2}\) let \(\ell^{(2)}\) be the scheme‑theoretic intersection
\(\ell\cap C\) counted with multiplicities.  A line \(\ell\) is **bitangent** to a smooth quartic
\(C\) if \(\ell^{(2)}\) consists of exactly two reduced points, each of multiplicity 2.

Define the closed subscheme  

\[
Z\subset U\times\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{2}\bigr)^{\vee}
\]

by  

\[
Z=\{\, (C,\ell)\mid \ell\text{ is a bitangent of }C \,\},
\]

where \((\mathbb{P}^{2})^{\vee}\) is the dual projective plane parametrising lines in \(\mathbb{P}^{2}\).
Let  

\[
\pi : Z\longrightarrow U
\]

be the projection onto the first factor.  
There exists a dense open subset \(V\subset U\) such that \(\pi\) is finite étale over \(V\).

For each prime \(p\) let \(\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) denote the number of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-rational points of \(V\), and define  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x),
\]

the limit of the average number of bitangent lines of a smooth quartic curve over the finite field \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\).  

Compute \(\bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor\).

Let  

\[
f(x)=x^{4}-2\in\mathbb{Q}[x]
\]

and denote by \(\Delta\) its discriminant.  
For a prime number \(p\) with \(p\nmid \Delta\) (so that \(f\) has four distinct
roots modulo \(p\)), let  

\[
N(p)=\#\{\,a\in\mathbb{F}_{p}\mid f(a)\equiv 0\pmod p\,\}
\]

be the number of solutions of \(f(x)\equiv0\pmod p\) in the finite field
\(\mathbb{F}_{p}\).

Define  

\[
L=\lim_{X\to\infty}\frac{1}{\pi(X)}\sum_{\substack{p\le X\\ p\nmid \Delta}} N(p)^{2},
\]

where \(\pi(X)\) is the number of primes \(p\le X\) with \(p\nmid\Delta\).

Compute \(L\) and give your answer rounded to **four decimal places**.  

(You may use without proof that the Galois group of the splitting field of
\(f\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\) is the dihedral group \(D_{4}\) of order \(8\), acting on
the four roots of \(f\) as the symmetries of a square.)

Let \(V\) be a 5‑dimensional vector space over a finite field \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\).  
Denote by \(\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)\) the Grassmannian of 2‑dimensional subspaces of \(V\); via the Plücker embedding \(\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)\) is realized as a smooth 6‑dimensional subvariety of projective space \(\mathbf{P}^{9}\).

For a fixed 3‑dimensional subspace \(W\subset V\) the condition
\[
U\cap W\neq\{0\}\qquad (U\in\mathrm{Gr}(2,V))
\]
is a hyperplane section of \(\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)\) in \(\mathbf{P}^{9}\).

Now choose **five** 3‑dimensional subspaces \(W_{1},\dots ,W_{5}\subset V\) in general position (so that the corresponding five hyperplanes intersect transversely).  
Let \(N(p)\) be the number of 2‑dimensional subspaces \(U\subset V\) satisfying
\[
U\cap W_{i}\neq\{0\}\quad\text{for all }i=1,\dots ,5 .
\]

Define
\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#\bigl(\text{choices of }(W_{1},\dots ,W_{5})\in (\operatorname{Gr}(3,V))^{5}(\mathbb{F}_{p})\bigr)} 
\sum_{(W_{1},\dots ,W_{5})} N(p),
\]
the average value of \(N(p)\) over all generic 5‑tuples of 3‑subspaces.

Compute \(\displaystyle \bigl\lfloor 100\,L \bigr\rfloor\).

(You may use without proof that the degree of the Grassmannian \(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)\) in its Plücker embedding is \(5\).)

Let \(C\subset\mathbf P^{2}\) be a smooth cubic curve defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic \(0\).  
Consider the projective space \(\mathbf P^{5}\) that parametrises plane conics (homogeneous degree‑\(2\) equations) up to scaling.  

Define  

\[
T=\Bigl\{[Q]\in\mathbf P^{5}\ \Big|\ 
\text{the conic }Q=0\text{ is tangent to }C\text{ at some point of }\mathbf P^{2}\Bigr\}.
\]

Show that \(T\) is a hypersurface in \(\mathbf P^{5}\) and determine its degree.  

Give your answer as a single integer (the degree of \(T\)).

Let \(G=G(1,3)\) be the Grassmannian of lines in projective three‑space \(\mathbb{P}^{3}\) over \(\mathbb{Z}\).  
For an ordered 4‑tuple of lines \(\mathbf{L}=(L_{1},L_{2},L_{3},L_{4})\) in \(\mathbb{P}^{3}\) define  

\[

Let \(\pi : Z\to (\mathbb{P}^{3})^{4}\) be the projection onto the second factor.
There exists a dense open subscheme \(V\subset (\mathbb{P}^{3})^{4}\) over which \(\pi\) is finite étale.

For each prime \(p\) let \(\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) denote the number of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points of \(V\), and for \(x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})\) let \(\#\pi^{-1}(x)\) be the number of \(\mathbb{F}_{p}\)-points in the fibre over \(x\).

Define  

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x).
\]

Compute \(L\) and give your answer rounded to four decimal places.  
(That is, output a decimal number with exactly four digits after the decimal point.)

Let  

* \(U\subset \operatorname{Hilb}^{3t+1}(\mathbf{P}^{2})\) be the Zariski‑open subset parametrising smooth rational plane cubic curves (i.e. irreducible plane cubics of geometric genus 0).  

* \(Z\subset U\times (\mathbf{P}^{2})^{8}\) be the closed subscheme consisting of tuples \((C,P_{1},\dots ,P_{8})\) such that each point \(P_{i}\) lies on the curve \(C\).

Denote by  

\[

\]

the projection onto the second factor.  
Let \(V\subset(\mathbf{P}^{2})^{8}\) be the dense open subset over which \(\pi\) is finite étale (equivalently, the eight points are in general position so that only finitely many smooth rational cubics pass through them).

For a prime \(p\) let \(\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})\) be the number of \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-rational points of \(V\). Define  

\[

Let  

\[
f(x)=\bigl(x^{3}-2\bigr)\bigl(x^{4}-3\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[x].
\]

For a prime \(p\) different from \(2\) and \(3\) the reduction \(f_p(x)\) is separable
over \(\mathbf F_{p}\).  Denote by  

\[

the number of \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-roots of \(f_p\).

\[

where \(\pi(X)\) is the number of primes \(\le X\).

Let  

\[
f(x)=x^{4}-2\in\mathbb Z[x].
\]

For a prime \(p\neq 2\) denote by \(N(p)\) the number of solutions of the congruence  

\[
x^{4}\equiv 2\pmod p
\]

in the field \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\) (counted without multiplicity).  
Define  

\[
L=\lim_{X\to\infty}\frac{1}{\pi(X)-1}\sum_{\substack{p\le X\\ p\neq 2}} N(p),
\]

where \(\pi(X)\) is the number of primes \(\le X\).  
Compute \(L\) and give your answer rounded to four decimal places.

Let  

\[
\begin{aligned}
F_2 &= X_0^{2}+X_1^{2}+X_2^{2}+X_3^{2}+X_4^{2},\\[2pt]
F_3 &= X_0^{3}+X_1^{3}+X_2^{3}+X_3^{3}+X_4^{3},\\[2pt]

\end{aligned}
\]

considered as homogeneous polynomials in the variables \(X_0,\dots ,X_4\) over the finite field \(\mathbb{F}_p\).

\]

Let  

\[
\pi : X \longrightarrow \mathbf{P}^{1}_{\mathbb{F}_p},
\qquad 
\pi\bigl([X_0:X_1:X_2:X_3:X_4]\bigr)= [X_0:X_1],
\]

be the projection onto the first two homogeneous coordinates.
Denote by  

\[
U \;=\; \{[a:b]\in\mathbf{P}^{1}_{\mathbb{F}_p}\mid a\neq 0,\;b\neq 0\}
\]

the dense open subset where neither coordinate vanishes.

For each prime \(p\) let  

\[

Define

\]

Compute the exact value of \(L\) and give it as a decimal number (no rounding is required).

Let  

\[
f(x)\in\mathbb{Q}[x]
\]

be a monic irreducible polynomial of degree 7 whose Galois group over \(\mathbb{Q}\)
is isomorphic to the simple group \(\operatorname{PSL}(2,7)\) (order 168).  
Via the natural identification \(\operatorname{PSL}(2,7)\cong\operatorname{GL}(3,2)\),
the group acts transitively on the seven non‑zero vectors of \(\mathbf{F}_2^{3}\);
this gives a permutation representation of degree 7.

For a prime \(p\) of good reduction (i.e. \(p\) does not divide the discriminant of
\(f\)), let \(\rho_p\) be the Frobenius conjugacy class in the Galois group.
The reduction of \(f\) modulo \(p\) has a linear factor over \(\mathbf{F}_p\)  
iff the corresponding permutation \(\rho_p\) fixes at least one point of the
7‑point set.

Assuming the Chebotarev density theorem, the set of such primes has a natural
density equal to the proportion of elements of \(\operatorname{PSL}(2,7)\) that fix
at least one point in this action.

**Compute this density and give your answer rounded to four decimal places.**

Let \(U\subset \mathbf P^{5}\) be the open subset that parametrises smooth plane conics (i.e. non‑degenerate quadratic forms) over a finite field \(\mathbb F_{p}\) \((p\) a prime\().\)

Fix a point \(P\in\mathbf P^{2}(\mathbb F_{p})\) and four distinct lines  
\(L_{1},L_{2},L_{3},L_{4}\subset\mathbf P^{2}\) defined over \(\mathbb F_{p}\) such that

* the four lines are in general position (no three are concurrent).

the limit being taken over all primes \(p\) for which the above genericity holds.

Let \(P^5\) be the projective space that parametrises all plane conics (including singular ones) in \(\mathbb{P}^2\).  
For a smooth conic \(C\subset\mathbb{P}^2\) define  

\[
H_C=\{\,D\in P^5 \mid D \text{ is tangent to } C\,\}.

is a zero‑dimensional scheme (i.e. a finite set of points, counted with multiplicity).

**Question:** How many points does \(Z\) contain? (Give the exact integer count.)

Let  

\[
f:\mathbb A^{2}_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow \mathbb A^{2}_{\mathbb Q},\qquad 
f(x,y)=\bigl(\,x^{3}+y,\;x+y^{3}\,\bigr).
\]

For a prime \(p\) let \(\mathbb F_{p}\) be the field with \(p\) elements.
Define  

\[
U_{p}=\Bigl\{(a,b)\in\mathbb F_{p}^{2}\;\Big|\;
\det\!\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x^{3}+y) & \frac{\partial}{\partial y}(x^{3}+y)\\[2pt]
\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x+y^{3}) & \frac{\partial}{\partial y}(x+y^{3})
\end{pmatrix}_{(x,y)=(a,b)}\neq 0\Bigr\}.
\]

Thus \(U_{p}\) is the set of \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-points of the largest open subset of \(\mathbb A^{2}\) on which \(f\) is étale.
